Check which clients reach each location of a store

Source: R/auth.R
store_auth_check.Rd

Tries every client the package uses for Google Cloud Storage with the credential of each location: Arrow (the file system that reads and writes data files), the JSON API (MD5 checksums), GDAL (rasters, through /vsigs/) and DuckDB (read_parquet() with a secret). Local folders need no credentials and give one row.

Usage

store_auth_check(st)

Arguments

st

A store connection from store_connect().

Value

A tibble with one row per location and client: location (the address), client ("arrow", "json_api", "gdal", "duckdb", or "all" for a local folder), ok (TRUE, FALSE, or NA when the client was not tried) and note ("ok", the error, or why it was not tried).

Details

Each probe is small: Arrow and the JSON API look up _catalog.parquet, GDAL opens the first raster file in the location's catalog, DuckDB counts the rows of _catalog.parquet. A failing client is reported, never raised. GDAL and DuckDB cannot use ambient credentials (no credential file found); their rows then say so. Opening a raster through GDAL gives GDAL's process-wide options the location's credential, as reading a raster does.

See also

rcs_auth_gcs() for the credentials and store_connect() to pass them; vignette("locations").

Examples

primary <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-auth-check")
st <- store_connect(primary, create = TRUE)
store_auth_check(st)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   location                                                    client ok    note 
#>   <chr>                                                       <chr>  <lgl> <chr>
#> 1 /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-aut… all    TRUE  loca…
unlink(primary, recursive = TRUE)
